messages:
Sasha (People Ops): FYI question from Marta - had to go to ER while on a company trip and paid out of pocket. Submitted expense, insurer paid part. What docs do we need to process the remaining reimbursement?

Marta (Product): Hi all - I paid 750 at a clinic in Madrid on 2026-04-02, insurer reimbursed 500. Uploaded the itemized bill + insurer EOB to Expensify. Do I need a separate form or manager note?

Liam (Finance): We can cover reasonable out-of-pocket emergency medical costs for approved travel. Required: itemized receipt showing services, insurer EOB showing amounts paid, brief incident statement (date/time/clinic/treatment), and manager approval. Also need to confirm the trip was company-approved.

Priya (Legal): Add: if insurer has a right of subrogation or already reimbursed the specific charge, we can't double-pay. EOB must show line-by-line. If employee signed over claim to us or waived insurer payment, we need that in writing.

Ravi (Manager): I approved Marta's expense in the workflow and added a note confirming this was a work trip.

Sasha (People Ops): Policy reminder: emergency medical after-hours during company travel are covered up to policy limits after personal insurance. Documentation must be submitted within 60 days of the incident.

Marta (Product): Done - I added an incident summary in the expense: "Fever and dehydration, ER visit at Clinica San Jose, 2026-04-02. Total paid 750, insurer paid 500 on 2026-04-05. Requesting 250." Attached receipts and EOB.

Liam (Finance): Thanks. I'll review the EOB for overlapping line items. If everything checks, we can run an off-cycle reimbursement to get you the 250 sooner. If insurer later reimburses you again for that same 250, we'll reconcile and may recover the overpayment.

expense-bot: :white_check_mark: Expense submitted (ID EXP-4927). Status: pending finance review.

Marta (Product): Prefer off-cycle, personal card already charged. Appreciate it! :pray:
file_note: Emergency medical reimbursement thread for travel; includes required docs checklist and policy timing.
